text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kurdish separatist guerillas claim responsibility for explosions at an ammunition factory which killed two and caused millions of dollars worth of damage.
- The newly formed government of Mesut Yilmaz is to award civil servants a 35 percent wage increase, instead of the planned 20 percent.
- Housing minister Yasar Topcu has said that a police intelligence officer, accused of tapping the telephones of the army top brass, also bugged the president's lines.
- Tansu Ciller's True Path Party will use party member and member former interior minister, Meral Aksener, as a scapegoat for the scandal erupting over police surveillance of the army.
- Left-wing leader Deniz Baykal, whose party's support is crucial to the new coalition, has criticised the government's reluctance to implement cumpulsory eight-year education.
- Turkey is considering building naval bases in northern Cyprus in response to a joint military doctrine between Greece and the Greek Cypriot controlled south of the island.
- After the munitions factory explosions at Kirikkale, attention has turned to other weapons and chemical factory installations sited close to populated areas.
